text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, even for someone who did not write it. One key idea is using clear naming conventions, so variables and functions have meaningful names. For example, a function called "calculateTotal" is much better than one called "doStuff". Functions should also be short and do only one job. This makes the code simpler to test and fix. Finally, clean code is easier to maintain over time, because other developers can quickly find and change parts of it without causing problems.
